measurements.source_locus: US 9,029,337 B2, Example 11, subsection "Clotting Analysis", Table 20 ("Effect of ISIS 403102 on PT and aPTT in BALB/c mice"), row 5 mg/kg, column "PT INR" (US9029337.txt line 12980)
measurements.verbatim_quote: TABLE 20 | Effect of ISIS 403102 on PT and aPTT in BALB/c mice | mg/kg | PT INR | aPTT INR | 5 | 1.09 | 1.05
measurements.notes: THE PT-SELECTIVE SIGNATURE OF THIS SOURCE: at 50 mg/kg PT reaches 4.37 INR while aPTT reaches only 1.16 INR. The patent draws the conclusion itself: "These data suggest that ISIS 403102 has a greater affect on the extrinsic pathway of blood coagulation than the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation." measurements.system_model: BALB/c mouse, FeCl3-induced inferior vena cava (venous) thrombosis model, Example 14
measurements.dose_unit: mg/kg per injection (twice weekly for 3 weeks)
measurements.timepoint: 30 minutes after FeCl3 application, 2 days after the last dose
measurements.control_description: PBS + FeCl3 control group set to 100 (a PBS - FeCl3 group is printed as 0 in the same table)
measurements.effect_vs_control: 34% of the PBS+FeCl3 thrombus PF-4 signal, i.e. a 66 percentage-point reduction in thrombus burden
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: treatment with ISIS 403102 resulted in a reduction of PF-4 in comparison to the PBS control. Therefore, antisense oligonucleotides are useful for inhibiting thrombus and clot formation.
measurements.source_locus: US 9,029,337 B2, Example 14, subsection "Quantification of Platelet Composition", Table 26, row 25 mg/kg (US9029337.txt lines 13481-13482)
measurements.verbatim_quote: TABLE 26 | Analysis of thrombus formation by real-time | RT-PCR quantification of PF-4 in the FeCl 3 | induced venous thrombosis model | mg/kg | PF-4 | PBS − FeCl 3 | 0 | PBS + FeCl 3 | 100 | ISIS 403102 | 25 | 34
measurements.notes: PLATELET-RELATED BUT NOT A PLATELET-COUNT ROW: PF-4 mRNA here is a surrogate for the platelet content of the excised vena cava thrombus, i.e. a measure of clot formation in a coagulation model, and the source states the coagulation interpretation explicitly. It is NOT a circulating platelet count and must not be routed to the thrombocytopenia endpoint.

measurements.system_model: Male cynomolgus monkey (2-4 years old, 2-4 kg), 13-week repeat-dose efficacy and tolerability study, Example 8

measurements.exposure_duration: up to 13 weeks of subcutaneous dosing

measurements.control_description: PBS-treated group of four cynomolgus monkeys on the same schedule; Table 52 is expressed as percent reduction relative to that control, so the control is 0% by construction and is not printed
measurements.effect_vs_control: 53% reduction in plasma prekallikrein protein relative to control at Day 17
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: NOT_REPORTED (the patent prints no severity or tolerability wording attached to Table 52 itself; the tolerability discussion is in Tables 53-57)
measurements.source_locus: US 9,670,492 B2, Example 8, Table 52 ("PKK protein level reduction (%) in the cynomolgus monkey plasma relative to control levels"), row ISIS 546232, column Day 17 (US9670492.txt line 62966)
measurements.verbatim_quote: TABLE 52 | PKK protein level reduction (%) in the cynomolgus | monkey plasma relative to control levels | Day 17 | Day 31 | Day 45 | Day 59 | Day 73 | ISIS 546232 | 53 | 58 | 72 | 75 | 70
measurements.notes: SCOPE CAVEAT: this is a plasma prekallikrein PROTEIN-LEVEL reduction (target engagement on a contact-pathway zymogen), not a functional clotting-time or amidolytic assay. It is included because prekallikrein is a coagulation-cascade factor and the depletion is the pharmacological mechanism behind the anticoagulant effect, but a curator wanting only functional coagulation assays should filter these rows out. The assay method for the protein measurement is not printed. ISIS 546828 shows 0% at Day 17 and ISIS 547927 shows 0% at Day 31, which are measured nulls at those timepoints. No SD, SEM or statistical test is printed for Table 52.

measurements.dose_unit: mg/kg per week (two subcutaneous injections per week for 3 weeks)
measurements.n_subjects: 10 per treated group (PBS control group was 8)
measurements.control_description: PBS-treated BALB/c mice (n=8) in the same table (US9670492.txt lines 65863-65865)
measurements.effect_vs_control: 0.03 mL vs 0.03 mL in PBS controls - identical to control
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: Treatment with ISIS 482584 did not significantly affect bleeding. These data suggest that the hemorrhagic potential of the compounds provided herein is low. These data taken with the results provided in Example 19 suggest inhibition of PKK with the compounds described herein are useful for providing antithrombotic activity without associated bleeding risk.
measurements.source_locus: US 9,670,492 B2, Example 20, Table 82 ("Tail bleeding assay after treatment with ISIS 482584"), row 20 mg/kg/wk (US9670492.txt lines 65870-65871)
measurements.verbatim_quote: TABLE 82 | Tail bleeding assay after treatment with ISIS 482584 | Dose | Bleeding | (mg/kg/wk) | (mL) | PBS | — | 0.03 | ISIS 482584 | 20 | 0.03
measurements.notes: THE BRIDGE FROM "CLOTTING CHANGED" TO "THE ANIMAL BLED": actual blood volume lost in a standardised tail-transection assay at three doses. NON-MONOTONIC: 0.03 mL at 20 mg/kg/wk (equal to PBS), 0.14 mL at 40 (4.7x PBS), 0.07 mL at 80 (2.3x PBS) - the peak is at the MIDDLE dose, which no dose-response model explains and which the patent does not comment on. No SD, SEM or statistical test is printed, so the "did not significantly affect bleeding" claim cannot be checked from the printed data. effect_direction records the source's own stated null rather than the arithmetic; unintended_toxicity is flagged true because bleeding is the liability this assay exists to detect, even though the source reports it as absent.

measurements.system_model: C57BL/6 mouse, single subcutaneous dose at Day 0, sacrificed Day 3; Serpinc1 (antithrombin) activity measured with a BIOPHEN anti-Factor Xa activity assay kit on diluted serum, Example 7
measurements.dose_unit: mg/kg, single dose
measurements.readout_unit: fraction of the PBS control (dimensionless ratio, 1.0 = control)

measurements.effect_vs_control: 0.099 of PBS control antithrombin activity (SD 0.021), i.e. approximately 90% knock-down

A single 10 mg/kg dose of AD-57213 led to an ED90 and a single 3 mg/kg dose led to an ED50.

measurements.verbatim_quote: TABLE 15 | AD-56813 optimized sequences and protein and activity levels. (The “Sense Sequence” column sequences are | disclosed as SEQ ID NOS 941-959, respectively, in order of appearance, and the “Antisense Sequence” | column sequences are disclosed as SEQ ID NOS 960-978, respectively, in order of appearance) | ELISA | Activity | Duplex | Sense | Sense | Antisense | 10 mpk | 3 mpk | 10 mpk | 3 mpk | name | ID | (5′ to 3′) | AS ID | (5′ to 3′) | Av | SD | Av | SD | Av | SD | Av | SD | AD- | 57213.1 | 0.098 | 0.021 | 0.264 | 0.032 | 0.099 | 0.021 | 0.255 | 0.030
measurements.notes: THE PROCOAGULANT DIRECTION: this is antithrombin (the body's main endogenous anticoagulant) being deliberately knocked down, so a LOW value here means LESS anticoagulant activity and a shift towards clotting, not towards bleeding. Assay is functional (anti-Factor Xa based), not an antigen ELISA - the matched ELISA antigen values for this same row are 0.098 (SD 0.021) at 10 mpk and 0.264 (SD 0.032) at 3 mpk, and were deliberately not written as separate measurement rows because they are protein levels rather than a coagulation function. UNIT AMBIGUITY IN THE SOURCE: the Table 15 caption calls these "activity levels" and the narrative at line 8133 calls the same screens "percent knock-down", but values such as 0.099 cannot be a percent - they are read here as fractions of the PBS control, which is the only reading consistent with the numbers. The source also prints the 3 mg/kg dose as "3 mg/mg" at line 8131, an obvious typographical error for mg/kg. The quote is the Table 15 header cells followed by this row's duplex-name cell and its eight numeric cells, joined with " | ", because the table survives the HTML-to-text conversion as one cell per line.

(The “Sense Sequence” column sequences are | disclosed as SEQ ID NOS 941-959, respectively, in order of appearance, and the “Antisense Sequence” | column sequences are disclosed as SEQ ID NOS 960-978, respectively, in order of appearance) | ELISA | Activity | Duplex | Sense | Sense | Antisense | 10 mpk | 3 mpk | 10 mpk | 3 mpk | name | ID | (5′ to 3′) | AS ID | (5′ to 3′) | Av | SD | Av | SD | Av | SD | Av | SD | AD- | 57213.1 | 0.098 | 0.021 | 0.264 | 0.032 | 0.099 | 0.021 | 0.255 | 0.030
measurements.notes: THE PROCOAGULANT DIRECTION: this is antithrombin (the body's main endogenous anticoagulant) being deliberately knocked down, so a LOW value here means LESS anticoagulant activity and a shift towards clotting, not towards bleeding. Assay is functional (anti-Factor Xa based), not an antigen ELISA - the matched ELISA antigen values for this same row are 0.098 (SD 0.021) at 10 mpk and 0.264 (SD 0.032) at 3 mpk, and were deliberately not written as separate measurement rows because they are protein levels rather than a coagulation function. UNIT AMBIGUITY IN THE SOURCE: the Table 15 caption calls these "activity levels" and the narrative at line 8133 calls the same screens "percent knock-down", but values such as 0.099 cannot be a percent - they are read here as fractions of the PBS control, which is the only reading consistent with the numbers. The source also prints the 3 mg/kg dose as "3 mg/mg" at line 8131, an obvious typographical error for mg/kg. The quote is the Table 15 header cells followed by this row's duplex-name cell and its eight numeric cells, joined with " | ", because the table survives the HTML-to-text conversion as one cell per line.

measurements.notes: THE PROCOAGULANT DIRECTION: this is antithrombin (the body's main endogenous anticoagulant) being deliberately knocked down, so a LOW value here means LESS anticoagulant activity and a shift towards clotting, not towards bleeding. measurements.system_model: Hemophilia A (F8-deficient) mouse, cremaster/microvessel laser injury model with intravital imaging; injury induced 10 days post-treatment, platelet and fibrin accumulation visualised and quantified, Example 14
measurements.delivery_method: injection (route not stated for this experiment; the compound is a GalNAc conjugate given subcutaneously elsewhere in the patent)
measurements.dose_unit: mg/kg
measurements.timepoint: 10 days after treatment, at laser injury
measurements.control_description: 0 of 13 injuries in the HA + PBS group; wild-type mice in the same table formed 10 stable thrombi from 10 injuries
measurements.effect_vs_control: every injury formed a stable thrombus (20/20) against zero of the untreated haemophilic controls; residual liver AT mRNA in this group was 50%
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: compound AD-57213 injected at 1 mg/kg or 30 mg/kg led to platelet and fibrin deposition leading to clot formation in 100% of the injuries
measurements.source_locus: US 9,376,680 B2, Example 14, Table 19, row "HA + 1 mg/kg ALN-AT3" (US9376680.txt lines 9998-10005)
measurements.verbatim_quote: TABLE 19 | Animals | Injuries | Stable | Percent AT | Group | (N) | (N) | Thrombus (N) | mRNA in liver | WT | 2 | 10 | 10 | 100% | HA + PBS | 2 | 13 | 0 | 100% | HA + 1 mg/kg | 4 | 20 | 20 | 50% | ALN-AT3
measurements.notes: CORRECTION OF A BLEEDING PHENOTYPE, i.e. the procoagulant direction of this endpoint: antithrombin knock-down restores clot formation in haemophilic mice. NOMENCLATURE NOTE: the Table 19 row labels print "ALN-AT3"/"ALNAT3" while the Example 14 narrative describes the same experiment as using "compound AD-57213"; the patent never states in words that the two names are the same compound, so the equivalence is recorded as an alias observation and not as a source claim. The counts are of injuries, not animals, and multiple injuries were inflicted per animal, so the injuries are not independent observations. Platelet and fibrin accumulation time courses for the same experiment are figure-bound (FIGS. 28A and 28B) and were not extracted.

measurements.notes: THE PROCOAGULANT FAILURE DIRECTION THE DATASET NEEDS. This is the single largest coagulation effect size anywhere in this bundle and it points towards thrombosis, not bleeding: knocking down the endogenous anticoagulant antithrombin raises thrombin generation up to four-fold in primates. readout_is_qualitative is true because "up to 4-fold" is a narrative upper bound over a set of figure-bound measurements, not a single measured value with a stated dose and timepoint. Do not treat it as a point estimate for any one dose group.

measurements.dose_unit: mg/kg, single dose

measurements.effect_vs_control: 50% suppression of antithrombin activity sustained for about 15 days
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: administration of compound AD-57213 leads to potent, dose-dependent suppression of Serpinc1 in HA mice with a single dose ED50 of less than 1 mg/kg on Day 7. Serpinc1 suppression was durable and correlated with the maximal level of antithrombin suppression achieved.
measurements.source_locus: US 9,376,680 B2, Example 9, US9376680.txt line 9581 (narrative summary of FIGS. 14-16)
measurements.verbatim_quote: As evidenced by FIGS. 14-16, administration of compound AD-57213 leads to potent, dose-dependent suppression of Serpinc1 in HA mice with a single dose ED 50 of less than 1 mg/kg on Day 7. Serpinc1 suppression was durable and correlated with the maximal level of antithrombin suppression achieved. A single dose of 1 mg/kg led to the maintenance of 50% suppression for about 15 days, while a dose of 10 mg/kg led to greater than 80% suppression maintained for 28 days.
measurements.notes: DURATION-OF-EFFECT for the anticoagulant protein being knocked down. The full day-by-day activity time course is figure-bound (FIG. 14, days 3, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 28 and 36) and was NOT digitised; only the two summary statements the text prints in words are recorded, which is why readout_is_qualitative is true and the timepoint field carries a duration rather than a single day.

extraction_notes:
WHAT THIS BUNDLE IS. Three granted US patents that carry on-target coagulation pharmacology for three different nodes of the
cascade: Factor VII depletion (Isis, US 9,029,337), plasma prekallikrein depletion (Ionis, US 9,670,492) and antithrombin
(SERPINC1) depletion (Alnylam, US 9,376,680). Two of the three lower clotting activity; the third raises it. That is deliberate -
the SERPINC1 source is the only one in this bundle whose effect direction is PROCOAGULANT.

THE PT-SELECTIVE SIGNATURE (S10). US 9,029,337 Table 20 is the centrepiece: ISIS 403102 at 50 mg/kg gives PT 4.37 INR while
aPTT reaches only 1.16 INR, and the patent itself draws the extrinsic-vs-intrinsic conclusion. Table 22 then follows a single
50 mg/kg dose all the way back to baseline (PT 1.11 at day 1, peak 1.97 at day 4, 1.12 by day 24, 1.10 by day 56), which is
reversibility/kinetics data that almost no literature source publishes. Every INR value in Tables 20, 22 and 24 is normalised to
the PBS group by the patent's own definition, so control_value is NOT_REPORTED and the PBS reference is 1.00 by construction.
No SD, SEM, per-group n or statistical test is printed for ANY table in this patent.

CONTRADICTIONS FOUND IN S10, RECORDED NOT RESOLVED.
 (a) Table 30 row label prints "ISIS 404071" while the Example 17 narrative that introduces the same six dose groups says
     ISIS 403102. ISIS 404071 occurs exactly once in the whole document and has no sequence anywhere in it. Those six bleeding
     rows are keyed to a separate oligo record named ISIS 404071 because that is what the table prints. They must NOT be silently
     merged with ISIS 403102, and no cross-document identification of ISIS 404071 has been imported.
 (b) The Table 24 preamble says the INR was computed for "the experimental group (i.e. 50 mg/kg treatment with ISIS 403102)",
     but Example 13 states every group in that study received 25 mg/kg. The 50 mg/kg wording is copied verbatim from the Table 22
     preamble. Dose recorded as 25 mg/kg per the Example 13 treatment paragraph; flagged on every affected row.
 (c) Example 16 describes four ISIS 403102 groups (5, 10, 20, 40 mg/kg) but Table 29 prints six rows (1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 40).
 (d) Tail-bleeding PBS baselines are not stable across experiments in this patent: 0.10 g (Table 27), 0.06 g (Table 30),
     0.22 g (Table 31). Absolute blood-loss values must not be compared across those tables.

S50 IS A BLEEDING SOURCE, NOT A CLOTTING-TIME SOURCE. The triage note was correct and has been enforced: aPTT appears exactly
once in all 66,176 lines of US 9,670,492, at line 1255, as embodiment/prospective language ("In certain embodiments, such
phenotypic changes include ... prolonged aPTT ..."). The strings "activated partial thromboplastin" and "prothrombin time"
appear zero times. NO aPTT ROW HAS BEEN EXTRACTED FROM THIS SOURCE; instead there is one explicit absence row recording the
silence. What IS measured is Table 82: blood volume lost in a standardised tail-transection assay at three doses, and the dose
trend is non-monotonic - 0.03 mL at 20 mg/kg/wk (equal to PBS), 0.14 mL at 40 (4.7x PBS), 0.07 mL at 80 (2.3x PBS). The patent
states "Treatment with ISIS 482584 did not significantly affect bleeding" but prints no SD, no n-adjusted test and no dispersion,
so that claim cannot be checked from the printed data. effect_direction on those rows follows the source's stated null while
effect_vs_control and notes preserve the arithmetic; unintended_toxicity is flagged true because bleeding is the liability the
assay exists to detect.

SCOPE DECISION ON PROTEIN-LEVEL ROWS. Table 52 of S50 (plasma prekallikrein protein reduction in cynomolgus monkeys, 9 compounds
x 5 timepoints) and the antithrombin antigen rows of S62 are coagulation-FACTOR-LEVEL readouts, not functional assays. They are
included because prekallikrein and antithrombin are named cascade components and because they are the exposure axis for the
functional effects, but every such row says so in its notes and can be filtered out by a curator who wants functional assays
only. By contrast, Table 19 of S10 (Factor 7 chromogenic assay), Table 78 of S50 (Spectrozyme FXIIa amidolytic assay) and the
Activity columns of Table 15 in S62 (BIOPHEN anti-Factor Xa antithrombin activity kit) ARE functional and are filed as
factor_activity without caveat.

PLATELET ROWS. Per the endpoint rules, no circulating platelet count has been extracted. Table 54 of S50 contains monkey
platelet counts and was deliberately left alone - it belongs to the thrombocytopenia endpoint. The PF-4 rows that ARE here
(S10 Tables 26 and 29, S50 Table 81) are real-time PCR measurements of the platelet content of an excised thrombus, i.e. clot
burden in a coagulation model, and each row says so explicitly so it cannot be mistaken for a blood count.

S62 PARSING: TABLE 15. This table wraps every sequence cell across four to eight physical lines and interleaves the sense and
antisense columns, so the fragments had to be reassembled. The reassembly was validated by an independent structural test: the
antisense base sequence must be the exact reverse complement of the sense base sequence plus a 2-nucleotide 3' overhang. 14 of
the 19 duplexes pass; 5 do not (AD-56741.2, AD-57203.1, AD-56475.3, AD-57209.1, AD-57207.1) and for those five NO SEQUENCE IS
ASSERTED - the sequence fields are NOT_REPORTED with the reason recorded on the oligo record. The numeric cells are unwrapped
and sit in fixed positions within each row, so all 19 rows' activity measurements are safe; the column assignment was further
confirmed by the fact that the table is sorted monotonically on the ELISA 10 mpk column (0.098 through 0.934).
AD-57213 passes and its sense/antisense reverse-complement relationship holds exactly, which is why it is the only compound for
which per-position modifications were written from this source.

S62 UNIT AMBIGUITY. The Table 15 caption calls the values "activity levels" while the narrative at line 8133 calls the same
screens "percent knock-down". Values such as 0.099 cannot be a percentage; they are recorded as fractions of the PBS control,
which is the only reading consistent with the numbers, and the ambiguity is flagged on every row. The source also prints the
3 mg/kg dose as "3 mg/mg" (line 8131), an obvious typographical error.

S62 NOMENCLATURE. Table 19 row labels print "ALN-AT3"/"ALNAT3" for the compound the Example 14 narrative calls AD-57213. The
patent never states the equivalence in words, so it is recorded as an alias observation on the oligo record, not as a source
claim. The name "fitusiran" does not appear anywhere in this patent and is not asserted here.

FIGURE-BOUND DATA WAS NOT DIGITISED. The per-dose peak-thrombin values (FIGS. 24A-D, FIG. 25), the Serpinc1 activity time
courses (FIGS. 13-16), the split-dose curves (FIGS. 17-19), the NHP protein time courses (FIGS. 21, 23, 26, 27) and the
platelet/fibrin accumulation curves for the laser-injury model (FIGS. 28A-B) all exist only as plots. Where the specification
states a number in words about a figure ("up to a 4-fold increase", "approximately 50, 70, 80 and >90% silencing", "50%
suppression for about 15 days"), that sentence is quoted and the row is marked readout_is_qualitative true. No value was ever
read off a plotted panel.

VERBATIM QUOTE CONVENTION. All three files are HTML-to-text conversions in which table cells survive as one cell per line rather
than as aligned columns. Quotes for table-derived rows are therefore the exact cell strings of the relevant header and data
cells, joined with " | ", with each cell's text reproduced character-for-character. US 9,376,680 additionally uses U+2003 EM
SPACE inside words such as "TABLE 15" and "AD-56813 optimized sequences"; those characters are rendered as ordinary spaces in
the quotes so that string matching against a normalised copy of the patent will succeed. Quotes for narrative rows are copied
straight from the sentence, including the source's own typographical errors (e.g. "portential" in US 9,376,680 line 499).

CITATION LIMITATION. None of the three FreePatentsOnline text conversions carries the named-inventor list, so the citation
strings identify each patent by title, assignee, number and dates only. No inventor name has been invented. The application
serial number for US 9,670,492 was not legible in the conversion and the fragment in that citation should be re-verified against
the USPTO front page before publication.
